name: Standing Single-Arm Cable Biceps Curl
grip: Supinated grip on D-handle with palm facing upward.
description: Flex one elbow to curl a low cable D-handle upward, maintaining constant cable tension on the biceps throughout the range of motion.
setup: Position the cable pulley at the lowest setting and attach a single D-handle.
Stand facing the pulley or slightly offset, grasping the handle in one hand with a supinated (underhand) grip.
Keep feet shoulder-width apart, knees softly unlocked, and upper arm pinned vertically to your side.
Non-working arm rests relaxed at your side or braced on your hip.
instructions: Curl the D-handle upward toward shoulder height by flexing the elbow, keeping the upper arm strictly stationary.
Squeeze the biceps firmly at the top of the curl without swinging the torso or letting the elbow drift forward.
Lower the handle slowly under control along the cable line until the elbow is fully extended.
Complete the desired repetitions, then switch to the opposite arm.
cues: Keep elbow pinned at your side.
Curl up smoothly against continuous cable tension.
Lower all the way down with control.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso or using hip momentum to start the curl.
Drifting the elbow forward, turning elbow flexion into front shoulder raise.
Cutting the bottom range of motion short.

logging.example: Cable pin set to 12.5 kg: record 12.5 kg selected stack load per side.
logging.note: Pulley mechanical advantages vary (often 2:1 on dual adjustable pulleys); record the pin setting on that specific station.

variantNote: Unilateral standing biceps curl using a low cable pulley and single D-handle, keeping upper arm stationary.
